linkedin.title: Most news apps treat personalization like a blunt instrument.
linkedin.body:
They show you stories based on what you clicked five minutes ago. That is not personalization. That is just chasing your last impulse. Real interest is subtler than that. It is about the topics you follow for years, the perspectives you value, and the depth of coverage you actually have time for.

At Headlinne, we built our recommendation engine to work differently. Instead of just tracking clicks, it maps the context of what you read. It looks at the nuance of the subject matter and how you engage with it over time. The goal is to filter out the noise so you only see the stories that genuinely add value to your day.

When you stop training an algorithm to feed your short-term curiosity and start teaching it to respect your actual interests, the experience changes. You spend less time scrolling and more time learning. It is a simple shift, but it makes the news feel like a tool again rather than a distraction.

story_card.headline: Polar oceans are changing fast
story_card.standfirst: A new report shows warming waters and shrinking ice are altering the planet's poles.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Arctic waters are warming rapidly. Sea ice is shrinking and wildlife is losing habitat.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Climate change is driving these shifts. It is causing record heatwaves across global seas.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The changes are happening at both ends of the planet. It threatens ecosystems globally.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future updates from the Copernicus Ocean State Report on long-term climate trends.

story_card.caption:
The Copernicus Ocean State Report reveals how climate change is reshaping the Arctic and polar oceans.

Rapid warming is causing sea ice to melt at an alarming rate. This shift is stripping away critical habitats for polar wildlife and disrupting ocean health worldwide.
